about: I design and operate the platforms behind engineering teams: cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes clusters, delivery pipelines, observability, and security controls.

At Lyric, I have helped build the engineering foundation from the founding stage through successive growth phases. My work includes an Internal Developer Platform, Argo CD workflows, and isolated preview environments for AI-assisted development.

I connect infrastructure decisions to operational outcomes: reducing cloud spend, making deployments repeatable, and integrating security into engineering workflows. My experience spans AWS, Azure, GCP, and earlier OpenStack and Ceph environments.

builds.name: SecretMesh: zero secret persistence
builds.text: SecretMesh separates secrets governance from secret storage. The control plane persists inventory and policy metadata; secret values remain in native cloud vaults. Identity, approvals, OPA policies, and audit records govern execution. A dedicated secret type is designed to prevent accidental logging or serialization.
builds.stack: Go · OPA · PostgreSQL (goose) · Keycloak · Moto · Next.js

builds.name: LitOverLap: RAG over academic literature
builds.text: As friendly help, I supported a friend with research tooling and its GCP infrastructure. Researchers upload a paper and see how it connects to an indexed corpus. PDFs become structured documents, then semantic chunks with BGE-M3 embeddings in Qdrant, plus a provenance-linked knowledge graph in Neo4j. I split it across three GCP VMs so heavy ingestion never blocks the API, with private networking and IAP-only SSH.
builds.stack: Python · Docling · BGE-M3 · Qdrant · Neo4j · GCP · Cloud NAT · IAP

prompts.title: Security as a design decision
prompts.text: Build SecretMesh as a cloud-native control plane with zero secret-value persistence. Secret values remain inside the customer's AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault or GCP Secret Manager. Redact them from logs, traces, error messages, crash dumps and telemetry.
